request: Welchen Anteil hat jeder meiner Supermaerkte an meinen Lebensmittelausgaben 2025?

plan.title: Anteil der Maerkte an den Lebensmitteln
plan.question: Ausgaben der Kategorie Groceries 2025 je Markt, die fuenf groessten einzeln und der Rest zu einer Zeile 'Sonstige' zusammengefasst, Spalten topic und total_eur.

sql:
WITH per AS (
  SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0 AND category IN ('Supermarket', 'Bakery')
  GROUP BY topic),
top5 AS (SELECT topic, total_eur FROM per ORDER BY total_eur DESC LIMIT 5)
SELECT topic, total_eur FROM top5
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Sonstige', ROUND((SELECT SUM(total_eur) FROM per) - (SELECT SUM(total_eur) FROM top5), 2)
reasoning_plan:
die Anfrage ist deutsch, also ist die Sprache de
sie fragt nach Anteilen an einem Ganzen, also ein Doughnut
die Lebensmittel sind die Unterkategorien Supermarket und Bakery
die Spalten sind topic und total_eur
reasoning_code:
the shape is doughnut, so pie allocates the slices and radialArc draws them
the columns are topic and total_eur, and total_eur is the value pie reads
the slices are the series, so color and key both name topic
a doughnut has no axes, so scales.x and scales.y are null and the legend is on

request: Compare December 2025 with November across the categories I spend the most in.

plan.title: December against November
plan.question: Spending of December 2025 and of November 2025 per category, one row per category and period, the period named 'This month' or 'Last month', the six largest categories by total over both months, columns topic, period and total_eur.

sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT CASE
           WHEN lower(description) LIKE '%rewe%' THEN 'Supermarket'
           WHEN lower(description) LIKE '%bvg%' THEN 'Travel'
           ELSE 'Rest' END AS topic,
         CASE WHEN booked_on >= '2025-12-01' THEN 'This month' ELSE 'Last month' END AS period,
         -amount AS eur
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on >= '2025-11-01' AND booked_on < '2026-01-01')
SELECT topic, period, ROUND(SUM(eur), 2) AS total_eur
FROM months
GROUP BY topic, period
ORDER BY topic, period
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
two periods are compared and the breakdown is by category, so two dimensions that cross
grouped bars put December beside November for each category
the period is the series and the category is the position, so the rows come long
an axis of names holds about six, so the six largest by total over both months
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_grouped, so barY carries a series and layout: group()
the columns are topic, period and total_eur, and total_eur holds the numbers
period is the series, so it is the z and the color channel and it needs a legend
category names on x on a band scale, none dropped and tilted, euros on y from the bare factory

request: Zeig mir pro Quartal 2025, wie sich meine vier groessten Kategorien stapeln.

plan.title: Vier Kategorien je Quartal
plan.question: Ausgaben je Quartal 2025 fuer die vier groessten Kategorien des Jahres, eine Zeile je Quartal und Kategorie, Spalten quarter als '2025-Q1', topic und total_eur.

sql:
WITH big AS (
  SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0
  GROUP BY topic
  ORDER BY SUM(-amount) DESC
  LIMIT 4)
SELECT '2025-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', booked_on) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3) AS quarter, coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0 AND coalesce(category, 'Needs review') IN (SELECT topic FROM big)
GROUP BY quarter, topic
ORDER BY quarter, topic
reasoning_plan:
die Anfrage ist deutsch, also ist die Sprache de
vier Kategorien ueber vier Quartale, zwei Dimensionen, die sich kreuzen
'stapeln' heisst, die Summe je Quartal zaehlt, also gestapelte Balken
die Anfrage nennt Quartale, also steht ein Quartal auf der Achse und kein Monat
die Spalten sind quarter, topic und total_eur
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_stacked, so barY carries a series and no layout
the columns are quarter, topic and total_eur, and total_eur holds the numbers
topic is the series, so it is the z and the color channel and it needs a legend
the bars are read off their own height, so the euro axis needs no grid

request: Compare how the spending on the joint account and on the personal one add up over 2025.

plan.title: Joint against personal, adding up
plan.question: Spending of 2025 added up over the months inside each account, one row per month and account, columns month as 'YYYY-MM', account and cumulative_eur.

sql:
WITH per AS (
  SELECT account, strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS eur
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0
  GROUP BY account, month)
SELECT month, account, ROUND(SUM(eur) OVER (PARTITION BY account ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur
FROM per
ORDER BY account, month
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
'add up' is a running total, which is an area, and 'compare' is a second one beside it
the account is the series, so one band per account and a legend
the two bands are read off the gap between them, so both start at zero
the columns are month, account and cumulative_eur
reasoning_code:
the shape is area and these rows carry a series, so one areaY and one lineY over all of them
the columns are month, account and cumulative_eur, and cumulative_eur holds the numbers
account names the series, so z and color on both marks and the legend goes on
an area rests on zero, so its euro axis is the bare scaleLinear factory
